title: Generic biextensions extend over a normal semiabelian base
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $P\to S$ and $Q\to S$ be smooth separated commutative group schemes of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], whose group operations satisfy the commutative group identities and whose diagonals are closed immersions. Assume every geometric fibre of each group is an extension, exact as fppf sheaves, of a proper smooth geometrically connected group scheme by a split torus $\mathbf G_m^r$, with $r\geq0$ (the ranks for the two groups and for different fibres may differ), where $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $S$, put $K=\kappa(\eta)$, and write $P_\eta,Q_\eta$ for the generic fibres [def-pc-base-change]. A $\mathbf G_m$-biextension of two commutative $S$-group schemes $(P,Q)$ means an invertible module $E$ on $P\times_S Q$ [def-sc-invertible-module], with trivializations on both identity axes agreeing at their intersection and isomorphisms $E_{x+x',y}\simeq E_{x,y}\otimes E_{x',y}$ and $E_{x,y+y'}\simeq E_{x,y}\otimes E_{x,y'}$. These are isomorphisms of pulled-back invertible modules on $P\times_SP\times_SQ$ and $P\times_SQ\times_SQ$, respectively; they satisfy associativity, commutativity and the identity laws in each variable, and the interchange law saying that expanding $E_{x+x',y+y'}$ in either order gives the same map to the tensor product of its four factors. Isomorphisms of biextensions preserve both laws and both axis trivializations. Tensor and pullback are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. Every $\mathbf G_{m,K}$-biextension $E_\eta$ of $(P_\eta,Q_\eta)$ is isomorphic to the generic restriction of a $\mathbf G_{m,S}$-biextension $E$ of $(P,Q)$. Every isomorphism between the generic restrictions of two such biextensions extends uniquely over $S$. In particular, the first assertion extends the underlying invertible module on the product together with both addition laws, not just its class modulo an equivalence relation.

external.place: Revised 2021 thesis Theorem 3.3.2.6 (printed p.70, PDF p.84), read online at https://www.kwlan.org/articles/cpt-PEL-type-thesis-revision-dense.pdf

proof.text: For any finite product $H$ of copies of $P,Q$, the structure map is smooth by smooth base change and composition [lem-pc-proper-base-change, lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Finite presentation and separatedness follow on affine charts and from the product diagonal. Each geometric fibre is semiabelian: take the product of the two exact sequences in the hypothesis, whose kernel is the product split torus and whose quotient is the product abelian variety. In particular its fibres are geometrically connected. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-group-vertical-cartier-descent] to $H$. We obtain the following full faithfulness for rigidified lines, also over the generic point. If $a_\eta:L_\eta\simeq M_\eta$ preserves the identity frames, it spreads to an isomorphism on $H_V$ for a dense open $V\subset S$: use finitely many local frames over a nonempty affine base open, clear denominators of the section, its inverse and their overlap equations, and shrink the base once. Its rational divisor $D$ is supported outside $H_V$. The cited divisor lemma says $D=p_H^*e_H^*D$. Along the identity its rational value is the isomorphism prescribed by the two global frames, so $e_H^*D=0$. Hence $D=0$; the same lemma makes $a_\eta$ an everywhere invertible section of $M\otimes L^\vee$. This gives a unique global rigidification-preserving isomorphism. Uniqueness follows from equality of rational sections on the integral scheme $H$.

proof.text: Work first over an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, and put $H=P_W\times_W Q_W$. Spread the underlying line $E_\eta$ and its trivialization at $(0,0)$ to $H_U$ for a nonempty principal open $U\subset W$. Here is the finite-data argument: choose finitely many principal affine charts of $H_\eta$ with line frames, lift their defining functions to charts of $H$ after localizing $R$, and clear the finitely many denominators in the transition units, their inverses and the triple-overlap equations. The charts cover after further shrinking because on each of a finite affine cover the generic cover admits a finite unit-ideal identity; clear the coefficients in those identities. The units now glue a line by [lem-pc-fpqc-descent](3). Its identity fibre and frame spread by the identical finite-chart argument on $W$. The generic biextension laws give a symmetry: $E_\eta(-x,y)\simeq E_\eta(x,y)^\vee$ by the first addition law at $x+(-x)=0$, and $E_\eta(-x,-y)\simeq E_\eta(-x,y)^\vee\simeq E_\eta(x,y)$ by the second. Spread this isomorphism and its inverse by clearing their finitely many coefficients. Thus the resulting rigidified line $N$ on $H_U$ is symmetric. Give it its unique cubical structure using [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification](b).

source.place: Sections 3.3.2 and 3.2.1; online revised thesis, printed p.70 (PDF page 84, zero-based index 83), Theorems 3.3.2.3(2), 3.3.2.6. Local copy WANTED. Agent assembly of the existing cubical-extension and descent statements.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-symmetric-cubical-extension] to $H\to W$ and $N$ on the dense open $U$. It supplies a cubical rigidified line $E_W$ on $H$ and a rigidification-preserving isomorphism $E_W|_{H_U}\simeq N$. Its generic restriction therefore identifies $E_W|_{H_\eta}$ with the supplied $E_\eta$. The normal integral locally Noetherian base and smooth separated finite-presentation semiabelian group hypotheses hold by step 1, while step 2 supplies the cubical structure and simultaneous-inversion symmetry. No positivity or properness assumption is needed.

source.place: Sections 3.3.2 and 3.2.1; online revised thesis, printed p.70 (PDF page 84, zero-based index 83), Theorems 3.3.2.3(2), 3.3.2.6. Local copy WANTED. Agent assembly of the existing cubical-extension and descent statements.

proof.text: Recover the full biextension data from this line. Restriction of $E_W$ to either identity axis is a globally rigidified line on $P_W$ or $Q_W$. Its generic trivialization extends uniquely by step 1. On $P_W\times_W P_W\times_W Q_W$, the two lines $(m_P,1)^*E_W$ and $\operatorname{pr}_{13}^*E_W\otimes\operatorname{pr}_{23}^*E_W$ are invertible and canonically rigidified at the total identity by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. Their generic addition-law isomorphism preserves that rigidification, so step 1 extends it uniquely. Apply exactly this argument on $P_W\times_W Q_W\times_W Q_W$ for the second addition law. On every axis of these products the required identity maps agree with the extended laws: both are extensions of the same generic maps. Associativity and commutativity in each variable are equalities of maps between the same invertible modules on products of at most four copies. The interchange law compares the two maps on $P_W^2\times_W Q_W^2$ to the four-factor tensor product. In each case the composites agree generically, and the products are integral by step 1, so their local coefficients agree as rational functions and hence as regular functions. All biextension axioms therefore hold over $W$.

proof.text: For two biextensions on $P\times_SQ$, their total-identity rigidifications and any supplied generic biextension isomorphism meet step 1. It gives a unique underlying line isomorphism extending it. Its compatibility with each axis trivialization and each addition law is an equality of regular maps on the corresponding integral product, true generically. Thus it is a biextension isomorphism. This proves the full-faithfulness clause independently of step 3. Finally cover $S$ by affine opens $W$. The extensions from step 4 are canonically identified on their overlaps by this full faithfulness. The identifications satisfy the cocycle condition, since the two composites have the same generic restriction. By [lem-pc-fpqc-descent](1),(3) the lines and their maps glue. The axis frames and addition laws glue by its full faithfulness, and their equations hold on the open cover. This produces the requested global biextension and its given generic identification.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q42-12606885f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item (statement unchanged; 5 steps; 0 new nodes) and all 7 cited statements in full. The statement matches Moret-Bailly II 3.6 and Lan Thm 3.3.2.6: generic restriction of G_m-biextensions of semiabelian groups over a normal integral base is an equivalence, here specialized by locally Noetherian and finite presentation. Neither source is local, both are WANTED, proof_origin is agent, and no SGA is cited. The former 5-node cycle is gone in the snapshot DAG: lem-sfb-symmetric-line-power-prolongation is unsplit and no longer cites raynaud-generic-ample-symmetrization, and no cited node's closure reaches the item. Step 1 meets every hypothesis of vertical-Cartier descent on finite products. The divisor of a frame-preserving generic isomorphism has e^*D=0, so D=p^*e^*D=0 and the isomorphism is everywhere invertible; uniqueness holds because H is integral. Step 2 writes out the finite-chart spreading argument (not a bare E5 'clear denominators'). The symmetry E(-x,-y)≅E(x,y) comes from the two addition laws with no division by 2, and cubical-rigidification (b) applies over a normal U. Step 3 applies symmetric-cubical extension to H=P×Q over affine W with exactly its hypotheses; this is a smaller input, not D1/D2. Step 4 extends both axis trivializations and both laws through step 1 on P²×Q and P×Q². The associativity, commutativity, identity and interchange equations hold by generic equality on integral products. Step 5 proves full faithfulness and glues over a Zariski cover by fpqc descent (1),(3), with the cocycle condition from uniqueness. Batch-5: lem-trf-smooth-composition is a generic Mathlib leaf. The closures of vertical-Cartier descent, cubical rigidification and symmetric cubical extension reach only generic trf/pod nodes (smooth-connected-fibre normal integrality, def-trf-algebraic-space, descent and limit lemmas). No trace-formula or Poincaré-duality theorem and no nt-assume leaf occurs, so all four are accepted. Accepted tool_uses: proper-base-change, smooth-composition, fpqc-descent and invertible-pullback-tensor, all generic. Unit and chapter unchanged. No fixes.
